chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Saeed ibn Janaah, from Abu Khalid al-Zaydi, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A group of people came to al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) and said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! We see in your dwelling things we dislike.' And in his house were rugs and cushions. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'We marry women, so we give them their dowries, and they buy whatever they wish. There is nothing for us from it.'

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Husayn have luxury items in his house if he was known for piety?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) clarifies that the furnishings in his home were acquired through the dowries (*mahr*) given to his wives, which became their exclusive property to spend as they pleased. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that a wife’s dowry is separate from her husband’s wealth, countering critics who viewed such domestic comforts as impropriety or extravagance. The incident underscores the practical application of marital financial rights within the Ahl al-Bayt's household.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from saeed Bin Janaah, from Abu Khalid Al Zaydi, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A group of people came over to Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>, so they said, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! We see such things in your<sup>asws</sup> dwelling which we dislike’, and in his<sup>asws</sup> house were rugs and cushions. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> marry women, so we<sup>asws</sup> give them their dowries, and they buy whatever they so desire to. There is nothing for us<sup>asws</sup> from it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Mansur ibn al-‘Abbas from Sa‘id ibn Junah from ibn Khalid al- Zaydiy from Jabir who has said the following: “

Once a group of people visited al-Husayn ibn Ali, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, and said, ‘O child of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, in your house we see such things that we dislike/ In his home there were pleasing spreading and cushions. He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘We marry women and give them their mahr (dower). They buy whatever they want and we do not have anything to say about it.’”
